import configparser
import textwrap

def _t():
    lines = textwrap.dedent('\n        [Foo Bar]\n        foo=newbar').strip().split('\n')
    parser = configparser.ConfigParser()
    parser.read_file(lines)
    assert 'Foo Bar' in parser, ('assertIn', 'Foo Bar', parser)
    assert 'foo' in parser['Foo Bar'], ('assertIn', 'foo', parser['Foo Bar'])
    assert parser['Foo Bar']['foo'] == 'newbar', ('assertEqual', parser['Foo Bar']['foo'], 'newbar')

import configparser

def _t():
    cfg = configparser.ConfigParser(inline_comment_prefixes=(';', '#', '//'))
    cfg.read_string('\n        [section]\n        k1 = v1;still v1\n        k2 = v2 ;a comment\n        k3 = v3 ; also a comment\n        k4 = v4;still v4 ;a comment\n        k5 = v5;still v5 ; also a comment\n        k6 = v6;still v6; and still v6 ;a comment\n        k7 = v7;still v7; and still v7 ; also a comment\n\n        [multiprefix]\n        k1 = v1;still v1 #a comment ; yeah, pretty much\n        k2 = v2 // this already is a comment ; continued\n        k3 = v3;#//still v3# and still v3 ; a comment\n        ')
    s = cfg['section']
    assert s['k1'] == 'v1;still v1', ('assertEqual', s['k1'], 'v1;still v1')
    assert s['k2'] == 'v2', ('assertEqual', s['k2'], 'v2')
    assert s['k3'] == 'v3', ('assertEqual', s['k3'], 'v3')
    assert s['k4'] == 'v4;still v4', ('assertEqual', s['k4'], 'v4;still v4')
    assert s['k5'] == 'v5;still v5', ('assertEqual', s['k5'], 'v5;still v5')
    assert s['k6'] == 'v6;still v6; and still v6', ('assertEqual', s['k6'], 'v6;still v6; and still v6')
    assert s['k7'] == 'v7;still v7; and still v7', ('assertEqual', s['k7'], 'v7;still v7; and still v7')
    s = cfg['multiprefix']
    assert s['k1'] == 'v1;still v1', ('assertEqual', s['k1'], 'v1;still v1')
    assert s['k2'] == 'v2', ('assertEqual', s['k2'], 'v2')
    assert s['k3'] == 'v3;#//still v3# and still v3', ('assertEqual', s['k3'], 'v3;#//still v3# and still v3')
try:
    _t()
except BaseException as _e:
    print('ORACLE_EXC ' + type(_e).__name__ + ' ' + repr(str(_e)))
else:
    print('ok')

import configparser
import io

def fromstring(string):
    cfg = configparser.ConfigParser(allow_unnamed_section=True)
    cfg.read_string(string)
    return cfg

def _t():
    cfg1 = fromstring('\n        a = 1\n        b = 2\n        [sect1]\n        c = 3\n        ')
    assert set([configparser.UNNAMED_SECTION, 'sect1']) == set(cfg1.sections()), ('assertEqual', set([configparser.UNNAMED_SECTION, 'sect1']), set(cfg1.sections()))
    assert '1' == cfg1[configparser.UNNAMED_SECTION]['a'], ('assertEqual', '1', cfg1[configparser.UNNAMED_SECTION]['a'])
    assert '2' == cfg1[configparser.UNNAMED_SECTION]['b'], ('assertEqual', '2', cfg1[configparser.UNNAMED_SECTION]['b'])
    assert '3' == cfg1['sect1']['c'], ('assertEqual', '3', cfg1['sect1']['c'])
    output = io.StringIO()
    cfg1.write(output)
    cfg2 = fromstring(output.getvalue())
    assert '1' == cfg2[configparser.UNNAMED_SECTION]['a'], ('assertEqual', '1', cfg2[configparser.UNNAMED_SECTION]['a'])
    assert '2' == cfg2[configparser.UNNAMED_SECTION]['b'], ('assertEqual', '2', cfg2[configparser.UNNAMED_SECTION]['b'])
    assert '3' == cfg2['sect1']['c'], ('assertEqual', '3', cfg2['sect1']['c'])
try:
    _t()
except BaseException as _e:
